pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a body-building food? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Rice
   C. Beans
   D. Chapati

2. Where should the holes in the pipe be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Only near the bucket
   B. Only at the end of the row
   C. Far away from the plants
   D. Next to each plant

3. What is a pin cushion used for? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting cloth
   B. Measuring cloth
   C. Keeping needles and pins safe
   D. Ironing cloth

4. Why is a hole dug before planting a tree seedling? (1 mark)
   A. To water the neighbours
   B. To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   C. To hide the seedling
   D. To give the tree shade

5. What is biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. Only wild plants
   B. Only birds
   C. A type of crop
   D. The variety of living things on Earth

6. Why should you wear gloves when handling compost materials? (1 mark)
   A. To make the compost sweeter
   B. So the heap grows faster
   C. To keep your hands cold
   D. To protect your hands from dirt and germs

7. What should you do with the fire when cooking is finished? (1 mark)
   A. Put it out
   B. Leave it burning
   C. Pour paraffin on it
   D. Add more wood

8. What is a wild animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal that lives freely in nature
   B. An animal kept for milk
   C. An animal kept in a house
   D. An animal sold in shops

9. Where should you buy fruit seedlings? (1 mark)
   A. A trusted nursery or agrovet
   B. From a stream
   C. From a scrap yard
   D. From anyone on the road

10. Where should kerosene be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In an open bowl
   B. In a water bottle on the table
   C. In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   D. Near the fire

11. What should you do with cleaning materials afterwards? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them on the floor
   B. Drink them
   C. Store them away from small children
   D. Give to animals

12. Why should dusters and mops be washed after use? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavy
   B. To make them smell
   C. So they do not spread dirt and germs
   D. So they wear out

13. What do protective foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Build walls
   B. Store water
   C. Help the body to fight sickness
   D. Give all the body's energy

14. Who should make holes in bottle caps and pipes with a nail? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or an adult
   B. A small child alone
   C. Nobody
   D. Anyone with wet hands

15. What is meant by income from animals? (1 mark)
   A. Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   B. Feathers
   C. Manure used
   D. Food eaten at home

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Describe how to make a scarecrow. (4 marks)

17. Compare a watering can with drip irrigation. (4 marks)

18. Describe how to prepare a class talk about one domestic animal. (4 marks)

19. Give three benefits of eating a balanced meal. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Beans
   Beans have protein.

2. D — Next to each plant
   Water must fall near the roots.

3. C — Keeping needles and pins safe
   It holds sharp objects.

4. B — To loosen the soil so roots can grow easily
   Loose soil lets roots spread.

5. D — The variety of living things on Earth
   Biodiversity includes all the different animals and plants.

6. D — To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   Gloves protect against germs and cuts.

7. A — Put it out
   Leaving fire burning wastes fuel and is dangerous.

8. A — An animal that lives freely in nature
   Wild animals are not kept by people.

9. A — A trusted nursery or agrovet
   Good seedlings are disease-free and true to type.

10. C — In a labelled container with a tight cap, away from children and fire
   Kerosene catches fire easily and is poisonous.

11. C — Store them away from small children
   Keep them safe.

12. C — So they do not spread dirt and germs
   Dirty tools spread dirt.

13. C — Help the body to fight sickness
   Vitamins and minerals help protect health.

14. A — A teacher or an adult
   Nails and awls are sharp and can cause injuries.

15. A — Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   Farmers sell products to earn money.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix a long pole firmly in the ground; tie a shorter stick across it; put a stuffed head on top; dress with a stuffed shirt and hat; add tins or shiny strips.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: A watering can wets a wide area and much water is lost by running off and by evaporation. Drip irrigation puts water beside the roots slowly, so less is used, fewer weeds grow, and the leaves stay dry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the watering can, 2 marks for drip irrigation.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose an animal; collect pictures; list its uses and care; practise speaking clearly; present and answer questions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives energy, helps the body to grow and repair, and protects from illness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.
